summary: X is worth ~30 min/day for Tideover, but treat the hype skeptically: most "build in public" and "X algorithm 2026" content surfacing in search is SEO-blogspam citing each other's numbers, not primary evidence — the real, verifiable build-in-public wins (Pieter Levels, Arvid Kahl, Jon Yongfook/Bannerbear) are consumer/indie tools built over years, not a 90-day niche-B2B analog. Two durable signals are worth building the system on: X's own ranking code has historically weighted replies far above likes (a reply the author replies back to is worth ~150x a like) and penalizes off-platform links 50-90%, so the daily system should be reply-first, not link-first. Separately, the tabletop/crowdfunding creator discovery layer (Rahdo Runs Through, BoardGameGeek, Discord, TikTok) lives mostly off X, so X functions here as a founder-to-founder and hardware/indie-hacker channel, not a backer-acquisition channel — calibrate expectations down accordingly. Realistic 90-day outcome for a no-audience solo founder at this cadence is a few hundred followers and pipeline arriving as DMs/replies from a handful of crowdfunding-creator peers, not a viral break. WISMO teardowns naming a specific struggling public campaign are a bad look — those creators are Tideover's exact customer segment — so default to anonymized/composite patterns, never named mockery. Cadence: one flagship post/day plus 15-20 minutes of reply engagement into hub threads, drafted by AI from Dylan's real daily notes and approved in under 10 minutes.

items.name: Typefully (Creator plan)
items.what: Drafting + scheduling tool with AI-assisted compose, works across X/LinkedIn/Bluesky.
items.how: Connect X account via OAuth; each morning paste Dylan's 2-3 sentence raw note into Typefully's AI compose, generate 3 variants in one of the 5 recurring formats, edit to voice, queue for a fixed daily time slot. Free tier (15 posts/mo, no AI) is a fallback if budget is cut.
items.cost: $19/mo Creator plan for AI writing + scheduling; $8/mo Starter has scheduling only; $0 Free tier capped at 15 posts/mo, no AI
items.risk: low — OAuth token scope only, no ban risk from scheduling itself

items.name: X Premium Basic
items.what: Cheapest paid tier; unlocks reply-priority ranking and a documented reach floor above free accounts.
items.how: Subscribe the Tideover account at x.com/i/premium_sign_up ($3/mo tier); skip the $8 tier unless the long-form (25k char) post format gets used regularly.
items.cost: $3/mo Basic (no long-form posts); $8/mo Premium for long-form + fuller boost
items.risk: low spend, but reported reach multipliers (6-10x impressions) come from third-party impression-scraping analyses, not disclosed X data — treat as directional, not guaranteed

items.name: Format: anonymized before/after support reply
items.what: Show a real (details-changed) risk-scored ticket next to the generic canned reply vs. the Tideover-drafted no-hard-date, confidence-band reply.
items.how: Pull from Dylan's own product output only (not a competitor's real customer without consent); strip identifying details; post as a 2-tweet before/after image or quote-style text.
items.risk: low — it's Tideover's own generated content; still confirm no real backer-identifying detail survives the anonymization pass

items.name: Format: founder story thread
items.what: The $2M gym-equipment company's COVID-era 60+ day waits, told in pieces over months rather than one dump.
items.how: Break docs/founder-story.md into ~10 story beats; post one every 1-2 weeks as a standalone post, always signed "— Dylan"; no fabricated numbers beyond what's already verified in the story doc.
items.risk: low — story already resolved as the credibility anchor per project memory

items.name: Format: behind-the-product build log
items.what: Short, specific updates on what shipped/broke this week in Tideover (mirrors the pattern behind Levels/Kahl/Yongfook's traction, adapted to vertical SaaS).
items.how: One line from Dylan on what changed (a feature, a bug fix, a customer reaction), no revenue-number fabrication — proof-only rule applies here same as customer-facing copy.
items.risk: low, bounded by the same proof-only doctrine as the rest of the product

items.name: Format: composite WISMO pattern post (not named-campaign teardown)
items.what: Describes a support/comms pattern seen across late campaigns generally, never a single identifiable named creator.
items.how: Draft as "saw this exact comment-wall pattern three times this month" rather than screenshotting/linking one specific Kickstarter/BackerKit page; if a real campaign is referenced, only ones already extremely public/viral and framed sympathetically, never mocking.
items.risk: MEDIUM-HIGH if done wrong — naming a specific struggling creator reads as ambulance-chasing against Tideover's own target customer segment and can permanently burn that relationship; default to the anonymized/composite version

items.name: Reply-first engagement into hub threads
items.what: 15-20 min/day replying into BackerKit's official account, Kickstarter Games discovery threads, #buildinpublic, and crowdfunding-creator hashtag activity.
items.how: Dylan keeps a running list of 10-15 accounts (BackerKit, active tabletop/hardware campaign creators, indie-hacker build-in-public accounts) and replies with real, specific input before or instead of posting; algorithm rewards author-replied-to replies far more than original posts with no discussion.
items.risk: low — but note the tabletop reviewer/influencer discovery layer (Rahdo Runs Through, BoardGameGeek, Discord, TikTok) is mostly off-X, so this channel reaches campaign creators and hardware/SaaS peers, not backer audiences directly

items.name: Native X scheduler (Grok compose / X Pro) as fallback
items.what: Free built-in scheduling if the Typefully subscription gets cut for budget reasons.
items.how: Use X's native compose scheduling (available to Premium subscribers) instead of Typefully; loses AI-assisted drafting, so Dylan writes from the same raw-note pipeline manually.
items.cost: free with X Premium Basic ($3/mo) already budgeted above

daily_actions.action: Dylan voice-notes or types 2-3 raw sentences on what happened today (a ticket, a build note, a comment-wall pattern) into the swipe file
AI drafts 3 post variants from the raw note, rotating through the 5 recurring formats, and queues them in Typefully
Dylan reviews the 3 drafts, edits one to voice, kills fabricated-sounding claims, approves for the daily slot
Dylan spends the first block replying with real, specific input into 5-8 hub/community threads (BackerKit, crowdfunding creators, build-in-public accounts) before posting
Dylan replies to comments/replies on yesterday's post to trigger the author-reply-back ranking signal
Weekly (amortized daily): pull one more real anonymized support exchange into the swipe file so the format doesn't run dry

load_bearing_claims.claim: X's ranking algorithm weights replies far above likes (a reply the author replies back to is worth roughly 150x a like), and posts with off-platform links see reach cut 50-90% — so a reply-first, link-averse posting habit is favored by the mechanics, not just etiquette.

X Premium subscribers see a substantially higher reach floor than free accounts (one impressions analysis of ~18.5M posts found free accounts averaging under 95 impressions/post vs. ~640 for Premium), though this is third-party analysis, not X's own disclosed methodology.

The tabletop/board-game creator discovery and influence layer runs mainly through YouTube reviewers (e.g. Rahdo Runs Through), TikTok, and BoardGameGeek/Discord communities rather than X, meaning X reaches campaign creators and hardware/indie-hacker peers more than backer audiences.

Research on brands publicly engaging with negative complaints found companies that responded publicly to negative tweets saw a drop in stock price and brand-image reduction, because it draws more attention to the complaint — supporting an anonymized/composite approach over named public teardowns.

The clearest evidenced build-in-public-to-customers pipeline (Pieter Levels' Photo AI: $5.4K in week one, $132K MRR by month 18) converted an audience built over roughly a decade of daily posting, not a 90-day cold start — this caps how aggressively 90-day pipeline expectations should be set.

Typefully's paid tiers ($8 Starter / $19 Creator with AI writing / $39 Team) and Hypefury's tiers (from $29, sweet spot $65) both fit inside the founder's $100-150/mo total tool budget individually, but Typefully Creator is the cheaper way to get AI-assisted drafting.
